author: agent:claude-code
message: MT7927 (X870) wifi/bluetooth support as core.wireless.chip; vgsquid-jade is the X870 box, so it moves to the latest kernel with tt-kmd 2.11.0; one of azul/onyx is the TUF X670E-PLUS WIFI; GNOME as a desktop session (user's request) (proposal 01a15f3a-d983-769d-859f-c1e84b748cce, proposed by agent:claude-code, accepted by user)

text: The board's wifi/bluetooth chip is a host switch, core.wireless.chip (none, mt7922, mt7927)
why: MT7927 (MediaTek Filogic 380, on the X870 boards) is driven by mt7925e only from kernel 7.2 (checked in nixpkgs: 6.18.57's mt7925e has no 14c3:6639/7927 alias, 7.2.11 and 7.3 do), with its wifi firmware in linux-firmware 20261019 and ASPM turned off by the driver itself. So mt7927 asserts kernel >= 7.2 and redistributable firmware. Its bluetooth firmware (mediatek/mt7927/BT_RAM_CODE_MT6639_2_1_hdr.bin, asked for by btmtk in 6.18 and 7.3) is not in linux-firmware yet (MR !946 waits on MediaTek's redistribution sign-off), so the module adds it from the MR author's pinned commit (sha256 669c5c99..., matches the published hash) when bluetooth is on. mt7922 (mt7921e, 14c3:0616/7922) needs nothing beyond linux-firmware on any kernel; the option records it and asserts the firmware.

text: Tenstorrent hosts run the latest kernel with tt-kmd 2.11.0; hugepages reserved at boot
why: nixpkgs 26.05's tt-kmd 2.7.0 fails on 7.2 and 7.3 (implicit zap_vma_ptes, checked), and vgsquid-jade's X870 MT7927 wifi needs 7.2+. tt-kmd 2.11.0 builds on 7.3 (checked), so the module installs it in place of nixpkgs' (hardware.tenstorrent's four lines, since that module always takes the kernel's tt-kmd) and falls back to nixpkgs' once it reaches 2.11.0. jade's full system builds with tenstorrent.ko and mt7925e for 7.3; not yet loaded on the card.

text: Headless server with a Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a (no GPU) on an X870 board (MediaTek MT7927 wifi), that colleagues log into over the tailnet with their own accounts.
Tenstorrent accelerators on NixOS: the tt-kmd driver (newer than nixpkgs' where it must be) and tools, the 1G hugepages the host runtime maps, and fixes for what nixpkgs ships broken.
GNOME is a third desktop session beside Plasma and Hyprland, under SDDM
why: The user asked for it as an option. With Plasma also installed, plasma6 and seahorse both set programs.ssh.askPassword, so ksshaskpass is forced; gcr-ssh-agent is off as under Hyprland because gpg-agent is the SSH agent. Evaluated on vgkraken with gnome alone, with plasma, and with all three; no host turns it on yet.

title: Took jade to share azul's and onyx's board, and guessed the X670E box
body: jade was described as the same base hardware as azul and onyx; it is the X870 (MT7927), and one of azul/onyx is the ASUS TUF X670E-PLUS WIFI. Lesson: a host's board is the user's fact; when it matters (wifi chip, kernel), ask or read lspci on the machine rather than carry it over from a sibling host.

title: Set core.wireless.chip on azul and onyx (and vgkraken) from lspci -nn once installed
body: One of azul/onyx is X870 (mt7927), the other the TUF X670E-PLUS WIFI (ASUS doesn't name its wifi 6E chip; mt7922 is likely). vgkraken's wifi 7 card is MT7925 or MT7927; MT7927's bluetooth needs this option for its firmware.

title: Drop the MT7927 bluetooth firmware fetch once linux-firmware ships it
body: linux-firmware MR !946 (mediatek/mt7927/BT_RAM_CODE_MT6639_2_1_hdr.bin). A build collision between the two firmware packages will show when it lands.
